title: Boss: a module three teams can use
summary: Make the site module work with for_each, release a minor version from its own repository with a tag and a changelog, then ship an internal rename that no caller notices.

steps.title: PLAT-202
body: *"Checkout, search and web all want the standard site setup. Platform owns the `site` module. Make it usable for all
three from one call, release it properly, and from now on no module release may replace anything in a caller."*
You are the module's maintainer and its first caller (`~/infra/platform`). Three steps.

steps.title: Incompatible with for_each
prompt: `~/infra/platform/main.tf` calls `./modules/site` with `for_each` over the three teams' domains. `terraform init` or
`plan` refuses. Read the error, fix the **module** (not the call), and apply the three sites.

checks.name: no provider configuration in the module
checks.fail: The module still configures a provider (a `provider "..." {}` block). Keep `required_providers`; remove the configuration.

checks.name: three sites applied
checks.fail: `terraform state list` should show a certificate in each of the three `module.site[...]` instances.

hints: *Module is incompatible with count, for_each, and depends_on* ... *contains provider configuration*: look in `modules/site/providers.tf`.
Empty `provider "tls" {}` blocks configure nothing useful, but they still make the module a "legacy module". The root module gets default provider configurations without any block.
`rm modules/site/providers.tf`, then `terraform init`, `terraform plan -out=tfplan`, `terraform apply tfplan`.
steps.explain: Since Terraform 0.13, modules declare providers (`required_providers`) and callers configure them. Old modules with `provider` blocks still work with a single call, which is why they linger, but they block `for_each`, `count` and `depends_on` on the call.

steps.title: Release v1.1.0
prompt: The module now lives in its own repository: your working copy is `~/src/tf-modules` (its `origin` is the team's
server, `/srv/git/tf-modules.git`). `~/infra/platform` uses it from Git at `v1.0.0`. The teams want each site's key
1. In `~/src/tf-modules`: add an output `cert_fingerprint` (with a description) to `site/outputs.tf`, add a `v1.1.0`
entry at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, commit, tag `v1.1.0` and push the commit **and** the tag.
2. In `~/infra/platform`: use `v1.1.0`, add an output `fingerprints` (team to fingerprint), `terraform init`, plan,

checks.name: v1.1.0 is released
checks.cmd: git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git show v1.1.0:site/outputs.tf | grep -q 'output "cert_fingerprint"' && git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git show v1.1.0:CHANGELOG.md | grep -q '1\.1\.0' && ! git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git show v1.0.0:site/outputs.tf | grep -q cert_fingerprint
checks.fail: The server should have a tag `v1.1.0` whose `site/outputs.tf` has `cert_fingerprint` and whose `CHANGELOG.md` mentions 1.1.0 (`git push origin main --tags`). `v1.0.0` must stay as it was.

checks.name: the platform uses v1.1.0
checks.fail: `.terraform/modules/modules.json` should show the site module at `?ref=v1.1.0`. Change `ref` and run `terraform init`.

checks.name: fingerprints output
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/platform && terraform output -json fingerprints | jq -e 'keys == ["checkout","search","web"] and all(.[]; startswith("SHA256:"))' >/dev/null
checks.fail: `terraform output -json fingerprints` should map checkout, search and web to `SHA256:...` fingerprints.

checks.name: nothing was replaced, plan clean
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/platform && for d in checkout.example.com search.example.com www.example.com; do test "$(stat -c %Y out/$d/nginx.conf)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/nginx-$d)" || exit 1; done && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null
checks.fail: A site's files were rewritten, or the plan is not clean. A new output should change nothing real.

hints: `git commit -am "Add cert_fingerprint output" && git tag v1.1.0 && git push origin main --tags`. A tag that is not pushed does not exist for anyone else.
In `~/infra/platform`: `sed -i 's/ref=v1.0.0/ref=v1.1.0/' main.tf`, an `outputs.tf` with `value = { for team, s in module.site : team => s.cert_fingerprint }`, then `terraform init`, plan, apply.
solution:
sed -i '0,/^## v1.0.0/s//## v1.1.0
- New output `cert_fingerprint`.

## v1.0.0/' CHANGELOG.md
steps.explain: An added output is a **minor** release: no caller has to change anything. Tags are the contract; never move or delete a published tag (every caller pinned to it would silently change). Registries (public or private) read the same Git tags to publish versions.

steps.title: v1.2.0: a rename no caller notices
prompt: The naming standard says `local_file.nginx` in the module should be `local_file.server_block`. Release that as
`v1.2.0` so that callers upgrading see **only moves**: in `~/src/tf-modules`, rename it, ship what makes it safe, add
a changelog entry, commit, tag `v1.2.0`, push. Then upgrade `~/infra/platform` to `v1.2.0` and apply. No site's file

checks.name: v1.2.0 renames with a moved block
checks.cmd: git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git show v1.2.0:site/main.tf | grep -q 'resource "local_file" "server_block"' && git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git grep -q -E 'from *= *local_file.nginx' v1.2.0 -- site && git -C /srv/git/tf-modules.git show v1.2.0:CHANGELOG.md | grep -q '1\.2\.0'
checks.fail: Tag `v1.2.0` on the server should rename the resource to `server_block`, include `moved { from = local_file.nginx  to = local_file.server_block }` in `site/`, and mention 1.2.0 in the changelog.

checks.name: the platform uses v1.2.0
checks.fail: Upgrade the call to `?ref=v1.2.0` and run `terraform init`.

checks.name: the state has the new names
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/platform && test "$(terraform state list | grep -c 'local_file.server_block$')" = 3 && ! terraform state list | grep -q 'local_file.nginx$'
checks.fail: Apply the upgrade: each `module.site[...]` should have `local_file.server_block` and no `local_file.nginx`.

checks.name: no file was rewritten, plan clean
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/platform && for d in checkout.example.com search.example.com www.example.com; do test "$(stat -c %Y out/$d/nginx.conf)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/nginx-$d)" || exit 1; done && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null
checks.fail: A site's nginx.conf was rewritten (the rename destroyed and re-created it), or the plan is not clean. Ship a `moved` block inside the module.

hints: Rename the block in `site/main.tf`, and add `moved { from = local_file.nginx  to = local_file.server_block }` in the module itself (for example `site/moved.tf`): it applies to every caller's state.
Changelog, `git add -A && git commit -m ... && git tag v1.2.0 && git push origin main --tags`.
In the platform: `sed -i 's/ref=v1.1.0/ref=v1.2.0/' main.tf`, `terraform init`, then the plan shows three *has moved to* and nothing else.
solution:
sed -i '0,/^## v1.1.0/s//## v1.2.0
- `local_file.nginx` is now `local_file.server_block` (a moved block is included: nothing is replaced).

## v1.1.0/' CHANGELOG.md
git commit -m "Rename local_file.nginx to server_block (with moved block)"
steps.explain: `moved` blocks inside a module are the module author's tool for refactoring without breaking callers. Keep them for a long time (until you are sure nobody upgrades from before), and treat any release that makes a caller's plan show `-` or `-/+` as a major version, with a migration note.
